citation.authors: Jafari A, Mardani H, Faghfouri AH, Fashtali ZM et al

record.population: 82 studies (79 quantitative and 3 qualitative; the title calls them randomised controlled trials), 5,026 participants, 1 to 48 weeks (doses 200 to 4,600 mg a day)
record.design: Systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis, GRADE-assessed
record.finding: Nigella sativa supplementation significantly improved body fat percentage, systolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, post-meal glucose, insulin sensitivity, C-reactive protein, cholesterol fractions and triglycerides. The authors conclude it could be a promising adjunct therapy for improving cardiovascular risk factors.
record.note: The abstract does not give the certainty grade or participants' ancestry; no safety summary read. Authors report no competing interests.
